title: 2026-12-29 Redwood throughput tuning deep dive with BrightScale
summary: Deep dive on throughput tuning for BrightScale's inference workload. Covered continuous batching behavior, scheduler knobs (max_num_seqs, max_tokens), KV cache warm vs cold, quantization impacts, and VPC/on-prem constraints. Agreed to run a short pilot benchmark with BrightScale's sample traffic and share recommended scheduler settings and benchmark script.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-29 15:00 PST | Duration: ~48 mins | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (BrightScale Head of ML), Elena Sokolov (BrightScale Infra), Tom Wu (BrightScale CTO)

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick intro then dive into throughput tuning — diego will lead the tech bits
[00:00:12] Raj Patel: yeah thanks Maya, we've got Elena and Tom on too, excited to see how your runtime handles our steady-state peaky traffic
[00:00:25] Diego Alvarez: cool, quick agenda: continuous batching behavior, scheduler knobs like max_num_seqs and token limits, kv cache warm vs cold, quantization knobs, and then on-prem / VPC notes. we'll sprinkle in some numbers from our benchmarks
[00:00:40] Elena Sokolov: quick note — our env is hybrid, helm-on-prem for latency-sensitive endpoints and cloud for batch; we care about 95th percentile <120ms for short chat flows ~32 tokens
[00:00:55] Diego Alvarez: got it. on continuous batching, the runtime tries to accumulate sequences up to max_num_seqs OR until max_latency threshold; so for low-latency chat you might set max_num_seqs lower or max_wait_ms lower
[00:01:10] Tom Wu: so max_num_seqs is per GPU queue or per worker?
[00:01:17] Diego Alvarez: per worker queue. if you have multiple workers on a node you'll see multiple batchers. also the scheduler has a priority preemption so short high-priority requests can cut in — but that adds overhead if mis-configured
[00:01:36] Raj Patel: we've been seeing long tails when traffic is bursty; is that due to KV cache cold misses?
[00:01:44] Diego Alvarez: partly yes. kv cache warmup matters: if you route different session ids across workers you'll lose prefix cache locality. for brightscale's use-case, pinning sessions or using sticky routing to worker groups improves cache hit rate
[00:02:02] Elena Sokolov: we do sticky for some endpoints but not all; sticky complicates autoscaling though
[00:02:10] Diego Alvarez: that's the trade-off. we recommend a small sticky window — e.g., 30s — which keeps most short chat sessions on the same worker but still allows scaling 
[00:02:26] Maya Chen: (interrupting) and if you can't sticky, increasing per-worker kv cache size helps but uses memory, and quantized models change memory profile too
[00:02:38] Raj Patel: about quantization — we saw +-5-7% latency delta with int8 vs fp16 in your public perf sheet, any gotchas on accuracy?
[00:02:49] Diego Alvarez: accuracy depends on model and post-training quantization. often int8 is fine for retrieval/assistant routing use-cases, less so for generation-sensitive scoring. we recommend running evals on critical prompts before wide quantization
[00:03:05] Tom Wu: how does continuous batching interact with max_tokens? If a request is long it blocks batching?
[00:03:14] Diego Alvarez: long sequences increase GPU time and can reduce batch count because worker is busy. we expose a max_tokens_per_batch setting and token-based scheduling so very long requests can be routed to a different queue or throttled to avoid head-of-line blocking
[00:03:31] Elena Sokolov: ok that sounds useful. do you expose these knobs via API config or inside the private deployment UI?
[00:03:39] Diego Alvarez: both. in Private you get the full set in the console and via YAML configs. hosted API exposes recommended profiles and some advanced knobs via admin API for enterprise accounts
[00:03:53] Raj Patel: can you walk through a recommended config for our profile: 100 rps peak, 20 tokens avg, bursts to 300 rps for short minutes?
[00:04:02] Diego Alvarez: for that, start with max_num_seqs=16, max_wait_ms=15, max_tokens_per_batch=1024. use preemption enabled for priority traffic. also set a small sticky window to keep kv cache warm for 80% of sessions. autoscaler min workers sized for baseline 100 rps, burst capacity via reserved burst pool
[00:04:28] Tom Wu: numbers check — with those knobs what's expected 95p latency for 20 tokens on an Llama 2-13B quantized to int8?
[00:04:38] Diego Alvarez: rough ballpark on our infra is 60–90ms 95p if cache warm and batching hits, rougher if cold. we should run the exact test on your sample workload to be sure
[00:04:52] Raj Patel: yes please run the test, we have a representative trace. we'll share it
[00:04:58] Elena Sokolov: question on VPC/on-prem — how do you handle KMS integration for model keys and audit logs? we have strict compliance needs
[00:05:07] Maya Chen: in Private we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations, audit logs to your SIEM, and SSO with SAML. we'll share the SOC2 + architecture doc after the call
[00:05:18] Tom Wu: any network recommendations to reduce tail latency for on-prem?
[00:05:23] Diego Alvarez: keep NLP workers and model stores on the same VLAN if possible, disable cross-rack shuffles for KV cache traffic; for hybrid setups, use a low-latency peered link to cloud and avoid high MTU fragmentation
[00:05:38] Raj Patel: sounds good. what about scheduler knobs for preemption overhead — we don't want lots of context switching
[00:05:46] Diego Alvarez: set preemption budget to a small percentage (5–10%) and prefer token-aware scheduling. we also have a mode that groups similarly sized sequences to reduce variance — that's the adaptive grouping scheduler
[00:06:00] Elena Sokolov: adaptive grouping — is that experimental?
[00:06:03] Diego Alvarez: it's GA in Private and in Dedicated; hosted has it behind an opt-in flag for now
[00:06:10] Raj Patel: ok, if we run your benchmark and the 95p is 180ms, what's the next tuning step?
[00:06:16] Diego Alvarez: first check cache hit rate; if low, sticky routing or increase cache size. second, reduce max_num_seqs to lower wait latency if you can afford fewer tokens per batch. third, consider model quantization or switching to smaller model variant for latency-sensitive flows
[00:06:31] Maya Chen: and we'll help run an A/B with identical prompts to quantify quality delta if you quantize
[00:06:37] Tom Wu: helpful. any common misconfigurations you see?
[00:06:40] Diego Alvarez: yep — setting max_num_seqs too high for chat workloads (leads to high median but sometimes better throughput), mixing sticky across multi-az without affinity, and not accounting for token distribution — spikes of long responses cause head-of-line blocking
[00:06:56] Raj Patel: about KV cache eviction — how deterministic is eviction policy? we need some predictability for long sessions
[00:07:03] Diego Alvarez: it's LRU by default with a tunable TTL; you can pin keys for VIP sessions, and there is a session affinity shim to avoid eviction for pinned flows
[00:07:15] Elena Sokolov: pinning helps but memory cost again — we'll share budget constraints in the sample trace
[00:07:20] Maya Chen: perfect, please attach memory budget to the trace, we'll size configs accordingly
[00:07:27] Raj Patel: one more — telemetry. we need token-level breakdowns and per-route traces for postmortems
[00:07:32] Diego Alvarez: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-model latency histograms, and tracing hooks that can integrate with Jaeger or your APM. we'll include an example dashboard export
[00:07:45] Tom Wu: ok let's talk pilot timeline; we can cut a 2-week pilot starting next week if you can run tests and give knobs 
[00:07:53] Maya Chen: we can. diego will run perf tests, I'll share the benchmark script and security docs. suggest start 2027-01-04?
[00:08:02] Raj Patel: that works for us, we'll prep the trace and sample keys
[00:08:07] Elena Sokolov: I'll also put together an infra yaml with node sizes and memory limits
[00:08:12] Maya Chen: great. quick recap of next steps in the call notes
[00:08:18] Diego Alvarez: (notes) run perf with max_num_seqs=16, max_wait_ms=15, max_tokens_per_batch=1024; enable adaptive grouping; run with int8 and fp16 for quality checks
[00:08:31] Raj Patel: thanks, that's helpful. any blockers we should be aware of for on-prem deploy?
[00:08:35] Diego Alvarez: just network peering and KMS access; if you have strict egress we can bundle offline installers
[00:08:43] Tom Wu: ok thanks everyone
[00:08:45] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and next steps

[end of captured transcript excerpt]
